Grade: Grade 5
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.6: Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you do to ensure you do not fumble while reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING PHONETIC AWARENESS MODELLING ENGAGEMENT PRONUNCIATION
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING PHONETIC AWARENESS MODELLING ENGAGEMENT PRONUNCIATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions

What this means
In this part you learn to apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you do to ensure you do not fumble while reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
